units.behavior_fact: Stores the inclusive lower and upper species base-stat-total bounds, without exchanging them.
Eligibility is a species-total inclusive range test.
Gendered individuals pass; genderless individuals in the Undiscovered egg group fail; remaining genderless individuals pass.
Retains the input eligibility condition for later inversion.
Inverts the supplied eligibility result.
Builds each tier using only its base-stat range and optional normal/inverse nonlegendary condition; the incoming challenge rule is unused here.

Nine tiers have the documented bounds. First filters by original single-member eligibility; rejects candidates in no tier. Selects an allowed tier from relative input position, then sorts inside each tier by total and species identity.
Repeatedly obtains rule-eligible candidates and rejects duplicates until the pool reaches 20. It does not truncate larger pools or impose a retry bound.

Different species cannot duplicate. Otherwise equal ordered four-slot move identities including nil, or equal item/nature/all-main-stat EVs, suffice. The temporary compaction/sort result is discarded.
Keeps input order, omits duplicates, and replaces the earliest same-species entry when admitting an eleventh distinct entry of that species.

Two-member rule copy governs construction and simulation; original rule returns for final tiers/allocation. Loads two independently rescued checkpoints, optionally seeds from existing content, runs eleven replacement/simulation cycles, keeps score strictly above 65, then publishes through trainer allocation. Checkpoints persist in multiple stages without a transaction.

Debug-only UI. No-list and existing-list prompts have different options/cancel mappings. Reuse migrates all nondefault challenge IDs and then writes data/PBS. New-generation confirmation precedes window creation; progress only refreshes at callback points; no mid-generation cancel or exception cleanup guarantee.
Adds all base-stat values of the species data.
Memoizes the species total by species identity.
Memoizes the baby species from the species data.
Memoizes the species minimum level.
Memoizes forward evolution records requested with the true filter parameter.
Uniformly samples move keys excluding the Struggle and target-last-move-copy function identities; no retry cap.

Processes level moves, machine-compatible tutor moves, and baby egg moves in order. Weights are first-actual-insertion sensitive. Pruning compares a prebuilt move-data snapshot while deleting from the actively traversed weighted list; self-deletion and order dependence are retained.

Has two explicit exclusions and ordered weight overrides, with zero-copy insertions allowing a later source to supply the move. Duplicate identities already in the weighted list block additional source weighting.
For a damaging candidate only, reports any higher-power same-type move in the whole supplied weighted list. It does not require equal function or accuracy.

Alternating species rejection bias; random EV emphasis and nature; 41-item list plus special gates; shared level-sensitive legal-move cache and Sketch mutation; short-move-list bypass; four-move combination gates; post-accept emphasis changes and item fixes; materialization at suggested level/IV31; final member eligibility is the only outer success exit.
Returns a copy of the species data type list.

Queries trainer and template tables separately. Empty trainers enter per-trainer shortcuts or a nonterminating ordinary draw. Normal nonempty input candidates are relabeled to original-rule suggested level without explicit stat recomputation. Builds preference weights, independent type trials, asymmetric index/member deduplication and sequential/random supplementation, then serializes all matches or a new list. Captures whether any default existed before scanning, saves data before writing PBS, and retains all earlier side effects on later exceptions.

Consumes a random pool member immediately for each required slot and retries complete construction until final team eligibility. Pool exhaustion is unguarded. Initializes active rating/history and zero cumulative games.
Returns the team member at the requested position.
Reports team member count for replacement, retirement and collection.
Exposes the active rating win-chance display value, not its raw rating.
Exposes the active rating record consumed when creating opponent snapshots.
Diagnostic tuple contains raw rating, deviation, volatility and display win chance; no in-scope normal caller found.
Diagnostic delegates comparison to an active rating operation that is not defined in the reviewed active rating record; no normal generator caller found.
Visible game count includes settled cumulative count (missing field treated as zero) plus pending history length.
Adds a result using an opponent-rating snapshot.
Pending game count is current history length.

Successful history settlement increases cumulative count by the number of removed history records. Counts are conserved; failures before clear do not settle the games and need not roll back rating fields.
Nonconsumed formatting helper uses conversions/fields that are not guaranteed by the active record; no normal generator caller found.
Nonconsumed helper interprets stored members as indices into another pool, unlike normal teams of creature objects; no normal caller found.
Stores opponent raw rating/deviation, score and K value; draw identity is negative one.
Stores empty pending matches and the associated active rating record.
Returns a pending match record by position.
Reports pending match count.
Enumerates pending matches in input order; available diagnostic enumeration has no separate normal caller.
Captures raw opponent rating/deviation at result insertion time. Later sequential settlement cannot retroactively change this snapshot.
Updates rating before clearing history. A propagated rating-update failure bypasses clear.
Unused alternative starts raw rating 1600 with zero deviation/volatility and absent display cache.
Unused alternative caches the stated logistic value; despite the helper name this is not promoted to a usable active generator percentage algorithm.
Empty input returns; nonempty input fails at acquiring undeclared current-match data. Active generation constructs the other rating record.
Active rating starts at raw 1500, deviation350, volatility0.9 and absent display cache.
Caches the display value; branches on deviation strictly above100 between the two independently described formulas.

Empty history inflates only deviation. Nonempty history computes snapshot factors/variance, excludes draws from improvement sum, updates volatility then deviation then rating, and writes rating/deviation/volatility in that sequence.
Converts raw rating to centered normalized scale.
Converts deviation using the same scale factor.
Computes the opponent deviation factor from the raw snapshot deviation.
Computes expected result from current normalized rating, opponent raw rating and factor.
Assigns updated volatility in its unchanged scale.
Writes denormalized raw rating and invalidates display cache.
Writes denormalized deviation and invalidates display cache.

Documented variation starts each update at current log volatility squared, uses system1.2 by default, limits to100 steps, stops on step-size tolerance and returns exponentiated half-final approximation.

Status moves score zero. Ground against Levitate stays neutral. Wonder Guard changes non-super-effective component factors to neutral before combining. The six-case discrete score matrix is used; unlisted products return zero.

For each own move and opposing member adds approximate type score, plus each own species total divided by10 with integer semantics and item bonus10. Adds scaled rating and a separate random0..31 draw for each side.
Scales and rounds both ratings before scoring; total-score ties compare these rounded values and then return draw5.

Random1% executes a no-visual AI-controlled noninternal real battle after suggested-level normalization and positional item snapshots; normal return heals and restores items but not normalized levels. Other99% estimates. Result1/2 versus other records win/loss or paired negative-one draws. Exceptions bypass subsequent recovery/result insertion.
